findings.evidence: “<target path> is the write target Step 2 resolved and already announced” starts a second explanation of the local default, global choice, and migration consent, after Step 2.1 already defines them.
findings.fix: Keep the target-selection and consent rules in Step 2.1. In Step 3 keep the operational handoff: reuse the recorded absolute path and pass only the replacement and backup flags that Step 2.1 authorized. Record the consolidation.

findings.evidence: “detects installed CLIs and models, proposes a review set and an execute set from the model catalog for the owner to pick, asks each role's priority order, effort and opt-in flags, then writes” leads with the wizard sequence. The valid description is 1,012 characters, with the user's intents and boundaries buried later.
findings.fix: Use when a user wants to set up, refresh, or check which AI models review or implement plans, or in what fallback order, even if they don't call them lanes. Configure ai-kit's [lanes] in ./.aikit/config.toml by default, using the installed CLI model catalog and the owner's choices for each role, effort, and opt-in flags. Announce the target and ask before replacing any roster; --local and --global select a target, not consent. Use --check-only to report availability without changing the lane config. Also use when ai-kit-spec-review or ai-kit-spec-execute-superpowers offers setup, an OpenCode lane's provider is no longer listed, or the owner asks about migrating review-spec.toml. Not for running configured lanes, hand-editing one lane, or editing [runner] or opencode.jsonc.

findings.evidence: “Step 1.6 — Sort unknown skills (optional)” loads the entire classification and role-write procedure even for check-only, migration-only, and setup runs that skip sorting. The 435-line body is already over 6,000 words before references are loaded.
findings.fix: Keep the branch condition and the distinction between advisory classification and owner-confirmed writes in the main flow. Put the classification output, prompts, commands, and independent-write report in a directly linked references/skill-role-sorting.md, loaded only when sorting is requested or the owner opts in. Keep the other conditional references where they are.

findings.evidence: “a role's review or execute table only when that role has a lane” gives no final gate when every candidate is declined or dropped and the owner also declines the session default. An in-memory render confirmed that an empty replacement removes both existing role arrays.
findings.fix: Before publishing, show the final lane count per role. If both counts are zero, stop by default; clear an existing roster only on explicit confirmation to clear it. Keep the earlier target and replacement consent checks.

findings.evidence: “its rows carry the label assumed: router-env alias naming and no rank or score, or an empty aliases list is stated” lets the router-alias case pass without ever exercising alias handling.
findings.fix: Give the eval a deterministic installed-runtime listing and catalog fixture that contain the alias. Require the exact pair to appear unranked and unscored, with no heuristic question. Keep the empty-group assertion in a separate case.

findings.evidence: “Create a new SKILL.md for a changelog generator from scratch” and the usage-metrics planning prompt are easy negatives in an otherwise strong set of 11 positive and 10 negative queries.
findings.fix: Replace those two generic negatives with realistic near-misses: diagnose an already-configured execute lane's quota error without changing the roster, and configure OpenCode's own default model without touching ai-kit's [lanes]. Record the replaced queries.

findings.evidence: “then stops with no writes” does not hold for the live check-only branch. The branch can probe without asking when every CLI profile says read-only, but the table-runtime probe goes through the supervised runner, whose ordinary live path sweeps and can remove stale host-run state outside the scratch directory. A CLI's read-only review mode does not make the runner read-only.
findings.fix: For an explicit no-change request, default to detection and non-spawning availability checks; mark unprobed lanes unknown. Before any live probe, distinguish no lane-config writes from runner and CLI side effects and get explicit consent.

findings.evidence: “On exit 2 with model catalog is empty, return to Step 1.5” can cycle indefinitely: when fetch is allowed but sources remain unavailable and nothing can be matched, fetching again can leave the catalog empty and yield the same exit 2. Only the no-fetch migration branch has a terminal fallback.
findings.fix: Allow one refresh. If the proposal still reports an empty catalog, show the source failures and offer an owner-confirmed model through the manual confirmation path, the session default, or stop. Do not re-enter the same fetch loop.

findings.evidence: “a command entry in this file or in the user config” points Step 4 to the global config.toml. Under global-merge, cfg_project_trust_bytes also reads the pending global review-spec.toml in memory when the user config has no roster. A matching legacy command key can therefore make a newly written project pair command-bearing even though Step 4 says it is active.
findings.fix: Use the same non-migrating user-lane lookup as the trust digest, including a pending legacy user roster when it is the effective source, and honor local-only. If trust is needed, leave the roster inactive unless the trust-flow preview and consent gates can be completed without an unapproved migration.

findings.evidence: “ARTIFICIAL_ANALYSIS_API_KEY=<key> to ~/.config/ai-kit/secrets.env” directs an owner with an absolute XDG_CONFIG_HOME to a file the fetch command does not read. local_secrets.secrets_env_path uses the XDG-aware directory.
findings.fix: Tell the owner to put the key in secrets.env beside the resolved user config, using the same XDG and home validation as the loader, or supply it as an environment variable. Keep the prohibition on the skill reading, writing, or displaying the key.

findings.evidence: “The owner adds it (it goes through wizard-flow.md steps 4 to 6 like any chosen lane ...), names another candidate, or says explicitly that there is none.” An added alternative can be declined at data-use confirmation or marked usage-limited itself; the text does not recheck that it actually qualifies before proceeding to write the role.
findings.fix: Recompute the role's fallback after the alternative completes its consent, usage-limit, and test steps. If the original lane is still stranded, ask for another candidate or an explicit no-fallback answer before writing.
